title: Request portfolio tiler and prioritization sparkline
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Objective: Create a lightweight, repeatable process and artifact (the 'tiler') that transforms a batch of Sales/CS enterprise feature asks into a tiled portfolio view and a one-line prioritization sparkline per tile. The output should enable PMs and Eng leads to do a 10–15 minute first-pass scoping and cost/benefit estimate for each tile and decide go/no-go for deeper discovery.

Scope: Non-bug enterprise feature requests collected from Sales/CS, Solutions Engineers, and AE outreach. We will not cover urgent incident requests, pricing/legal asks, or small UX polish items. Focus areas include Dedicated capacity features, Private/VPC capabilities, Console/observability features, and API/SDK enterprise controls.

Deliverables: 
- A templated tile format (title, problem, ideal account profile, expected value, rough effort bucket, risk flags, dependency list, proposed rollout guardrails).
- A prioritization sparkline (1-line assessment summarizing impact vs effort vs risk) and a short rationale.
- A 10-minute facilitator script for Sales/CS + PM alignment sessions to produce tiled portfolios for weekly triage.
- Example run with a real CS batch (anonymized) to validate throughput and decision quality.

Why: Current intake artifacts are inconsistent and require large PM time to normalize. A tiled portfolio approach groups similar asks, surfaces cluster-level economics, and reduces duplication of discovery work. The one-line sparkline gives executives and Eng leads a fast read for capacity planning and Dedicated commitments.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Simplicity vs fidelity: Tiles intentionally sacrifice exhaustive detail for speed. We accept more false negatives (deprioritized items that later resurface) to reduce triage time.
- Structured vs open intake: We will not enforce a hard form at first; instead we implement a light transform step run by Solutions Ops to produce tiles from free-text requests. If throughput demands, we will iterate toward a stricter intake form.

Operational steps: 
1) Solutions Ops exports the weekly CS ask batch into a Google Sheet template.
2) Facilitator runs a 30–60 minute tile-generation workshop with 2 PMs + 1 Eng lead to produce up to 12 tiles.
3) PM owns scoring and sparkline assignment, tags tiles for deep discovery or backlog.
4) Tiles and sparklines are pushed into the intake board (Linear) and the Console roadmap bucket for subsequent sizing.

Success metrics (30/60/90): 
- 30 days: Reduce average PM normalization time per ticket from ~40m to 12m (measured via time logs).
- 60 days: 50% reduction in duplicate discovery work across similar customer asks (measured by cluster dedupe rate).
- 90 days: Improve first-pass accuracy (tiles that required no pivot after discovery) to 65% from baseline ~45%.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Tile template file exists in Drive and is used to convert at least three weekly batches.
2) A completed example portfolio (>=6 tiles) derived from Sales/CS data is attached.
3) PM+Eng workshop runbook written and validated by Solutions Lead.
4) At least one tile advanced to discovery with estimated points and a documented dependency list.
5) Metrics collection instrumentation (time-to-normalize, dedupe rate, first-pass accuracy) has a dashboard entry or a spreadsheet with baseline and ongoing updates.
